events.title: Proposed ruling: refund_partial $6.27 (model confidence 0.82)
events.body:
This is a RydeTAXI trip (metered, total charged $31.22, distance fare $18.37 for 13.03 km) [F7], so RD-2's metered branch applies and the refund is limited to the distance units attributable to non-exempt off-route segments. The off-route segment 18:34–18:45 measured 5.53 km where the optimal route covers 1.08 km, adding 4.45 km [F3]; the overall excess of 5.30 km billed $7.47 at $1.4098/km [F1][F4]. The distance rate for this trip, per the fare record, is distance_fare ÷ distance_km = $18.37 ÷ 13.03 km = $1.40983/km [F4][F7][RD-2].

The detour is not excused by traffic: the only speed-band fact on the replaced stretch is Kampong Bahru Road band 2, and RD-4(b) forbids a band record standing alone as a ground for exemption; no incident satisfies RD-4(a) [F11][F14][RD-4]. Nor is it a rider-requested stop: nothing in the record has the rider naming any place or the car stopping anywhere, so RD-3(a) is not met [F8][RD-3].

Consent (RD-5) fails. The only rider-side consent the record could carry is the driver's own statement that the rider did not object, written after the trip — a driver's claim of agreement that appears only in his statement is not consent (G11) [F10][RD-5]. The only chat message is the driver's 18:30 question asking whether he may go round via Zion Road, and the chat record is complete with every message timestamped, so no rider message sent before the segment's 18:34:05 start exists [F8][F9][F3]. Even had the rider agreed by silence, the request was a specific road/area ("via Zion Road") whose scope cannot be tied to the driven path on this record (no road names for the driven path, and the fare/segment record places the deviation up to 1889 m off the optimal route), which under RD-5/G13 would be undetermined — and here the underlying consent itself is absent, so the reading that settles the case is that no rider consent exists and the segment counts. Segment F3 therefore counts; the remaining 0.85 km of the overall excess (5.30 − 4.45) is the corridor/jitter difference that RD-2 takes across the route corridor and does not refund [F1][F3][F4][RD-1][RD-2].

Amount: 4.45 km × $1.40983/km = $6.2738 ≈ $6.27 [F3][F4][RD-2]. The billed waiting fee $0.11 (0.4 min × $0.26/min) is a metered waiting unit on a RydeTAXI trip and is retained (RD-3(c)) [F5][RD-3]. No surge applied (1.0×) and no unpublished charge appears, so FARE-1 yields nothing further [F6][RD-1][FARE-1]. RD-6 does not apply: the driver's profile shows 1 upheld dispute in 90 days but 0 upheld route disputes, so this case is not "repeated" for route deviation and no account flag issues [F17][RD-6]. The rider's profile (2 disputes, 0 upheld) plays no part in the ruling [F16].

Safety screen: I read the complaint, both chat lines and the driver's statement. The complaint is a fare/route grievance; the driver's message is a route proposal; nothing contains a threat, intimidation, harassment, sexual remark or dangerous-driving allegation, so no SAFE-1 or SAFE-2 escalation arises [F8][F10][SAFE-1][SAFE-2]. Evidence is sufficient: the segment is measured, the fare record yields the rate, the chat record is complete and fully timestamped [F3][F4][F9].

events.title: Notices sent to rider and driver
events.body:
RIDER: We've reviewed your fare dispute and are refunding $6.27 as a Ryde voucher on your account.

We found you were taken off the shortest, most direct route for about 11 minutes on your trip, and the driver didn't have a valid reason or your agreement for that detour. The refund covers the extra distance from that detour at the rate you were charged. The rest of your fare stands.

The voucher is applied to your Ryde account automatically — no action needed. No further review of your account is being made, and this ruling doesn't count against you in any way.

DRIVER: We've reviewed the route dispute on this trip and are refunding the rider $6.27 as a Ryde voucher.

The trip record shows you left the shortest and most direct route for about 11 minutes and added extra distance to the fare. There is no sign of traffic or an incident that would explain it, and the rider didn't agree to that detour — asking in chat and getting no answer doesn't count as consent. Nothing was found that would make this an excuse.

Your account is not being flagged: you have no prior upheld route disputes. No change to your account standing, and no further action needed from you.

Even had the rider agreed by silence, the request was a specific road/area ("via Zion Road") whose scope cannot be tied to the driven path on this record (no road names for the driven path, and the fare/segment record places the deviation up to 1889 m off the optimal route), which under RD-5/G13 would be undetermined — and here the underlying consent itself is absent, so the reading that settles the case is that no rider consent exists and the segment counts. Segment F3 therefore counts; the remaining 0.85 km of the overall excess (5.30 − 4.45) is the corridor/jitter difference that RD-2 takes across the route corridor and does not refund [F1][F3][F4][RD-1][RD-2].
